section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the entire psalm recited before the shofar blast, especially the verse "Yivchar Lanu," relates to the transition from the Throne of Judgment to the Throne of Mercy, and that the shofar draws down mercy from the level of G‑d's essential choice of Israel, which is beyond arousal from below. Now, from the fact that before the shofar blast they recite (not only this verse, but) the entire psalm, it is understood that all the verses of the psalm are related to the matter of "He arises from the Throne of Judgment and sits on the Throne of Mercy," which occurs through the shofar blast. And certainly the verse "Yivchar Lanu" etc., which is adjacent to the verse "Alah Elokim B'Teruah" etc., indicates that this verse is connected to "Alah Elokim B'Teruah" etc. And it must be understood: The matter of "Yivchar Lanu" is that the Holy One's choice of Israel is from His own essence (and not that the service of Israel arouses Him to choose them), and moreover, the matter of this choice is in the Awtsmoos, where the concept of arousal from below does not apply. That is to say, in addition to the fact that the actual choice is from His own essence and is not aroused by arousal from below, rather, in this place (where the matter of choice is found) it is entirely impossible to arouse anything through arousal from below. And the matter of "Alah Elokim B'Teruah" etc. is, that the shofar blast of Israel arouses that He should arise from the Throne of Judgment and sit on the Throne of Mercy. And from the juxtaposition of the two verses, it implies that these two matters are connected to each other. That is to say, that by Israel taking their shofars and blowing before the Holy One, they draw down not only the mercy that is aroused through service (arousal from above that is awakened by arousal from below), but through this they also draw down the mercy that stems from the Holy One's choice of Israel, "Yivchar Lanu."

This section explains that the shofar blast on Rosh HaShanah draws down from the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof to renew the world and invest the kingship with pleasure and will, as the world is in a state of faintness before the coronation. 3) And it may be added, that the above matter (that by Israel blowing the shofar they also draw down the aspect of the choice of the Awtsmoos, where it is impossible to arouse through arousal from below) is also understood from what is known that the essential matter of Rosh HaShanah is the building of Malchus, as the Sages said, "Recite before Me [verses of] Kingship, so that you make Me King over you." And what they said, "The mitzvah of the day is with the shofar," is because the matter of "you shall make Me King over you" is through the shofar blast, as follows from the above statement of the Sages: "And with what? With the shofar." And the connection of Rosh HaShanah to the building of Malchus (simply) is, because on Rosh HaShanah is the renewal of the act of Creation. As we say, "This day is the beginning of Your works," for on every Rosh HaShanah all the worlds are brought into being anew, just as they were the first time. And the matter is, that the coming into being of all the worlds is from the attribute of His Kingship. And the drawing down of Malchus on each Rosh HaShanah (including also the first Rosh HaShanah at the beginning of Creation) is only for one year, and on the eve of Rosh HaShanah at nightfall it returns and ascends and is absorbed into its source. However, the ascent and removal is only in the inwardness of Malchus, which is the pleasure and will within Malchus. And the vitality of the world on Rosh HaShanah (even before the matter of "you shall make Me King over you") is from the externality of Malchus, analogous to a person who does work when he is tired and weak-handed, having no pleasure in it. And as per the well-known saying, that on the night of Rosh HaShanah (before the matter of "you shall make Me King over you") the world is in a state of fainting. And this is [the meaning of] "Recite before Me [verses of] Kingship, so that you make Me King over you," that He should have will and pleasure in the kingship. And it is known that the removal on Rosh HaShanah is in all levels (action, speech, thought, emotions and intellect), for all things return to their original state. And the drawing down of Malchus (will and pleasure in kingship) on Rosh HaShanah is by drawing from the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof. And from the fact that the matter of "you shall make Me King over you" is through the shofar blast as above, it is understood that the shofar blast reaches the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof.

This section raises a question: since the shofar blast is a mitzvah, which applies only after G‑d is made King, how can it be used to coronate Him? It concludes that the shofar has two aspects: the mitzvah itself, and the ability to reach the Awtsmoos beyond the aspect of King. And it must be understood: The shofar blast is a mitzvah, and the matter of commandments (mitzvos) applies specifically after He has become King, as the statement, "Accept My Kingship first, and then I will decree decrees upon you," and in order for there to be "you shall make Me King over you" (that Israel make Him King) it is by reaching the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof, as it is before (above) He becomes King, so how is it possible that through the shofar blast (the fulfillment of a mitzvah and command of the King) they should make Him King? From this it is understood that in the shofar blast there are two matters: the mitzvah of the shofar blast, and this [other matter] that through the shofar blast one reaches the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof, which is above the aspect of King.
